items.title: 67619_Big Nick Nicholas oral history interview
items.q: this fella, George Starks, who was assistant music director at the university... he found out I was in town, see, so he says, 'Why don't you come on over here,'

ctx.x: Had there ever been another context that you did something like that in before the University of Virginia came along?

No. I thought of it because I had to do one class in the big auditorium, Cabel Hall, for like 350. And then I had to do a workshop type tying in another hour. And this fella, George Starks, who was assistant music director at the university, he plays a little saxophone and what not and he found out I was in town, see, so he says, 'Why don't you come on over here,' 'cause he just came in. So that's how that happened. It was very successful and I started with the history of the saxophone and the different styles,…

he wrote a tune for me called 'Big Nick' and that seemed to bring me out of the woodwork a little bit, because the college students they were very fond of John Coltrane and they wrote several books on his life and I was in the books. So they were curious about me, you know what I mean. So that's how that got started, you know. So I did all these things for the children, which was a very rewarding experience for me, because children are so innocent and so lovely, you know what I mean. They'd really give me a lift,…
